reasoning: According to historical records from the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the US Congress has not passed all of its regular annual appropriations bills on time (prior to the October 1 start of the fiscal year) since Fiscal Year 1997 (which was enacted in late September 1996). Since FY 1998, Congress has consistently failed to meet the October 1 deadline for all individual regular appropriations bills, instead relying on temporary continuing resolutions (CRs) or late-enacted omnibus spending packages to keep the government funded.
